subject.title: improve(android): make Wear store releases reproducible

question: Should the repository preserve existing Android phone version codes ending in 50–99, or intentionally require release operators to migrate them before adopting the paired-Wear allocation policy?
rationale: The branch changes a previously accepted persisted release identifier and the safe migration cannot be inferred: renumbering published Android artifacts may conflict with Play ordering, while retaining legacy acceptance changes the desired long-term allocation contract.

options.title: Preserve or migrate legacy codes
options.body: Retain acceptance for already-configured 50–99 phone codes or add a narrow, documented migration and regression coverage before applying the 01–49 rule to new releases.

options.title: Accept a breaking release-operator change
options.body: Land the 01–49 restriction as-is only after explicitly documenting the required operator action and confirming it is safe for every supported Play release state.

options.title: Pause the allocation-policy change
options.body: Keep the manifest and proof work but defer the suffix-range restriction until a maintainable version-code allocation policy is approved.

recommendation.title: Preserve or migrate legacy codes
recommendation.body: Retain acceptance for already-configured 50–99 phone codes or add a narrow, documented migration and regression coverage before applying the 01–49 rule to new releases.

likelyOwner.reason: The original merged Wear architecture owns the paired phone/Wear release contract that motivates the new allocation policy.
